title: IMDS Launches Comparative Study with 228 Indicators Across All 27 Brazilian States
subtitle: Institute of Mobility and Social Development Releases Dataset Covering All Federation Units
excerpt: The Institute of Mobility and Social Development (IMDS) released a comparative study this Thursday (17), compiling 228 indicators from all 27 Brazilian states.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Institute of Mobility and Social Development (IMDS) launched a comparative dataset this Thursday (17), encompassing all 27 Brazilian federation units. The material compiles information organized into 228 indicators, enabling the standardized analysis of various aspects across the states.

The indicators are categorized across various areas, although the summary does not detail what these specific areas are. The initiative aims to provide a reference tool for anyone needing to compare performance and characteristics among states, facilitating analyses that consider multiple dimensions simultaneously.

By making this data available, IMDS contributes to transparency and access to information that can support decisions in public policy, planning, and research. The comparative study is accessible for public consultation, allowing managers, students, and other interested parties to explore the results according to their needs.

With information from Agência Brasil.
